methods.label: Bound the game counts and test the possibilities
methods.explanation:
A team has three opponents in its own division and four in the other division. Its schedule therefore satisfies
\[
3N+4M=76,
\]
where \(N\) and \(M\) are whole numbers of games. These two groups account for every game in that team's schedule exactly once.

Since \(N>2M\), its three same-division series contain more than \(6M\) games. Hence
\[
76=3N+4M>6M+4M=10M,
\]
so \(M<7.6\). Together with \(M>4\), this leaves only \(M=5,6,7\).

For these three values, the number of games left for the team's own division, \(76-4M\), is respectively \(56,52,48\). This number must split equally among three opponents. Only \(48\) is divisible by \(3\), giving \(N=16\) and \(M=7\).

These values satisfy \(16>2\cdot7\) and \(7>4\). Thus a team plays \(\boxed{48}\) games within its own division, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: A simple schedule equation bounds the search to three whole-number possibilities; only elementary inequalities and divisibility are needed.
